data.narrative:
Orqa is a Series A–stage drone and autonomous systems company that has raised approximately $22M to date. The broader Drones & Autonomous sector includes eight private peers of varying stages and scales—including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro—but no directly comparable public benchmarks. The heterogeneity of this peer set limits conventional multiples-based approaches.

Valuation analysis relied on stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation approach given sparse same-stage and same-tier private comparables. Using total capital raised ($22M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A–to–subsequent-stage transitions yields an implied valuation of $44M. This method assumes Orqa's capital deployment and operational progress to date justify a doubling of entry value, consistent with venture-stage progression patterns.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $37M (low) to $51M (high), with $44M as the median point. Key uncertainties include: the absence of narrow-peer revenue or growth metrics to anchor relative-value methods; stage-specific multiplier sensitivity in an early-stage, capital-intensive sector; and the composition risk inherent in a sector where outcomes cluster at extremes (outsized winners versus capital-constrained outcomes). Any revision would require either additional same-stage or recent Series B comparables with disclosed financials, or disclosure of Orqa's own revenue, burn rate, or unit economics.
